data.name: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC)
data.description: Cancer of the kidney; target indication for everolimus treatment in clinical practice.
data.description_beginner: The most common form of kidney cancer. It's an approved use for the mTOR-blocking drug everolimus in clinical practice.

studies.title: Efficacy of everolimus in advanced renal cell carcinoma: a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled phase III trial

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Everolimus extended median progression-free survival from 1.9 to 4.0 months versus placebo in metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

studies.title: Defining the role of mTOR in cancer

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Comprehensive review arguing mTOR signaling is commonly deregulated in human cancers, laying out the rationale for rapalog trials in oncology.

studies.title: Temsirolimus, interferon alfa, or both for advanced renal-cell carcinoma

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Temsirolimus alone extended median overall survival to 10.9 months versus 7.3 months with interferon alfa in poor-prognosis metastatic kidney cancer; rash, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia were more common with temsirolimus.

relations.mechanism: RECORD-1: everolimus roughly doubled progression-free survival after other targeted therapy failed.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In a clinical trial, everolimus roughly doubled the time before advanced kidney cancer got worse, after other treatments had stopped working.
relations.boundary: Second-line setting, after VEGF-targeted therapy - not first-line.

relations.mechanism: Renal cancers frequently carry lesions that leave mTORC1 constitutively active - which is why this tissue responds to mTOR inhibitors at all, and why an exceptional responder could be traced to TSC1 loss.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Many kidney cancers carry mutations that leave mTORC1 stuck "on" – that's why this cancer type responds to mTOR-blocking drugs at all, though it doesn't prove mTORC1 causes the cancer.
relations.boundary: Correlative plus one n-of-1 genomic case (IYE2012); not a demonstration that mTORC1 activation initiates RCC.
relations.note: Replaces TUMOR-RCC, which asserted 'Tumor growth activates RCC' - a category error, since RCC is an instance of tumour growth, not a downstream target.

relations.mechanism: In poor-prognosis renal cancer, temsirolimus improved overall survival against interferon - the hardest endpoint there is.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In hard-to-treat kidney cancer, temsirolimus helped patients live longer compared with an older drug.
relations.boundary: Poor-prognosis patients specifically; the combination arm did not beat temsirolimus alone.
relations.note: Overall survival, not a surrogate. Worth pointing at.
